entries.speaker: sonic-youth
entries.found: Nobody else in the band gave a rat’s ass about Sparks! So we really connected – we were Sparks fanatics.
entries.citation: Thurston Moore, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2025): "I was really into Sparks. Nobody else in the band gave a rat's ass about Sparks! So we really connected – we were Sparks fanatics."
entries.note: Fandom during his Sonic Youth years (Jim O'Rourke era), not a formative-years claim; borderline, owner may prefer favourite.

entries.speaker: omd
entries.found: “It changed my life. I went to see them on September 11, 1975, at the Liverpool Empire, and I sat in Q36.
entries.citation: Andy McCluskey of OMD, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2023), on Kraftwerk's 'Autobahn': "It changed my life. I went to see them on September 11, 1975, at the Liverpool Empire... it really was the first day of the rest of my life."

entries.speaker: omd
entries.found: Like the rest of the country, I had just seen David Bowie and The Spiders From Mars on Top Of The Pops the week before when [presenter] Dave Lee Travis said ‘get a load of this’. We’d seen glam, but British glam – Slade and The Sweet – were like builders in sequins. And there was Bowie looking like this androgynous lizard thing, that was a real wow factor.
entries.citation: Andy McCluskey of OMD, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2023), on buying Ziggy Stardust at 13: "And there was Bowie looking like this androgynous lizard thing, that was a real wow factor."
entries.note: Weak: a thrilled teenage first album purchase, not a claim about his own music. Owner may prefer favourite.

entries.speaker: spoon
entries.found: The Violent Femmes were probably the biggest band for me in that burst of new freedom, I just completely related to their lyrics. The lyrics speak to the minds of high school students like no other record – insecurity, anger, masturbation, frustration and lust.
entries.citation: Britt Daniel of Spoon, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2020), on 'Kiss Off' as the song that changed his life: "The Violent Femmes were probably the biggest band for me in that burst of new freedom, I just completely related to their lyrics."

entries.speaker: spoon
entries.found: When that moment hit me I was just finding out about Eric B. & Rakim, The Beastie Boys were just coming out, I was really into The Cure.
entries.citation: Britt Daniel of Spoon, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2020), on turning 15 in Texas: "I was really into The Cure."
entries.note: Passing mention of fandom at 15; thin, owner may prefer favourite.

entries.speaker: wire
entries.found: At the time being a Nick Drake fan was a very lonely life, but I was always into him.
entries.citation: Colin Newman of Wire, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2015), on buying an Island sampler with Nick Drake on it as his first album: "At the time being a Nick Drake fan was a very lonely life, but I was always into him."
entries.note: Thin: a youthful fan, no link to Wire's own music stated.

entries.speaker: ride
entries.found: ‘I Wanna Be Your Dog’, Iggy & The Stooges: “It was the first song we ever jammed and it always reminds me of the early Ride sound as that album was one of our big early influences.”
entries.citation: Andy Bell of Ride, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2015), on 'I Wanna Be Your Dog': "It was the first song we ever jammed and it always reminds me of the early Ride sound as that album was one of our big early influences."

offMap.name: Weezer
offMap.sentence: I butchered those songs lots of times, so maybe he did! (first album he bought as a young teen; "encapsulated teenage counterculture to me"; played live covers of Weezer)

offMap.name: The Moody Blues
offMap.sentence: Hearing it, I was like, ‘Oh that’s what I’m trying to do. The Moody Blues: you understand me’. I’m obsessed with it.

offMap.name: Harry Nilsson
offMap.sentence: I’m a huge Harry Nilsson fan and he’s one of my great inspirations

offMap.name: The Beatles
offMap.sentence: My mother had quite a cool collection of singles and she had quite a lot by The Beatles and The Kinks. (loved 'Thank You Girl' as a child; OMD recorded an unreleased cover)

offMap.name: Harry Nilsson
offMap.sentence: It just happens to be the first single I ever bought as well.

offMap.name: Kiss
offMap.sentence: Even though I didn’t play an instrument yet, I knew I wanted to be on that stage.

offMap.name: The Beatles
offMap.sentence: I was trying to learn to play guitar and sing at the time. (bought Meet The Beatles with The Beach Boys, "equally important")

offMap.name: The Byrds
offMap.sentence: I listened to those records all day long, but especially this one. (on 'Turn! Turn! Turn!', age seven or eight)

offMap.name: The Rolling Stones
offMap.sentence: Me and my friend Desmond had a band around 1970 – we used to listen to ‘Get Yer Ya-Ya’s Out’. (his song that made him want to be in a band)

offMap.name: The Rolling Stones
offMap.sentence: Something about ‘19th Nervous Breakdown’... got me really excited, and made me feel like I needed to make records.

offMap.name: The Beatles
offMap.sentence: That, and the whole Beatles catalogue. (made him feel he needed to make records)

offMap.name: Andrea McArdle
offMap.sentence: I sang along to that song so much that I got the lead in the school play and sang it onstage to a stuffed dog. (song that made her want to make music)
